findings.summary: THE MEASURED NUMBER IS WRONG BY 3x, AND IT IS THE NUMBER THE WHOLE DESIGN ARGUMENT RESTS ON. Four places now state 'three M4 commits landed with SKIP=check-reviewed': review.md:48-49 ('Measured on M4: three commits landed that way'), scripts/check-reviewed.sh:54 ('Three commits in M4 landed that way'), the M4.21 backlog row ('Three M4 commits landed that way'), and ReviewRoundCapTest.java:27-28 ('Measured on this milestone: three commits landed that way'). Measured: `git log --format='%h %s' --grep='SKIP=check-reviewed'` returns NINE commits, all of them M4, and every one of the nine bodies names rule 12's round cap as the SOLE remaining refusal -- 0837f34 M4.0, 44400b5 M4.1, 74254f6 M4.3, d9a3c22 M4.3b, 6871e7f M4.4b, 3a5ed79 M4.6c, 461dd53 M4.6e, 2953b5a M4.19, 2e0f1d9 M4.20. The likely source of 'three' is that M4.6c/M4.19/M4.20 call themselves the first/second/third time, which is itself an undercount of the six that preceded them.
findings.failure_scenario: The number is load-bearing in two opposite directions and it is now frozen into a STANDARD. It is the evidence that the missing escape made the gate absent (nine, not three -- the argument is stronger than stated), and it is simultaneously the baseline against which rule 12's own next paragraph -- 'a growing list of rounds: entries is a signal, not a workflow' -- will be judged. A future reader who sees the fourth `rounds:` entry appear will compare it against 'three' and conclude the escape is being over-used, when the measured pre-change rate was nine in one milestone; or, reading it the other way, will conclude the cap only rarely bit and that the escape was unnecessary. Either way the reader is calibrating against a figure this repository's own git log contradicts in one command, and non-negotiable 4 is the rule that a measured claim must have been measured.

findings.summary: THE INDEX-VS-WORKTREE READ IS UNPINNED, AND THE BACKLOG ROW CLAIMS IT IS PINNED. The M4.21 row says the five tests are 'each falsifiable against its own mutation of the gate -- cap removed, cap at 1, the task ignored in the key, and the worktree read instead of the index'. The first three hold. The fourth does not. Measured: replacing `git show ":baselines/review.txt"` at check-reviewed.sh:64 with `cat baselines/review.txt` and re-running anUNSTAGEDArgumentDoesNOTLiftTheCap's exact scenario still exits 1 (FAIL 'review round 3 exceeds ... cap of 2'), so the test still passes and the mutation SURVIVES. The reason is that the fixture builds its scratch with baseline==null, so baselines/review.txt is absent from the index ENTIRELY and the staged-NAME guard at check-reviewed.sh:63 refuses before the read is ever reached -- the test constrains line 63, not line 64. The distinguishing case was constructed and measured: baselines/review.txt committed and STAGED for a legitimate `reviewer:R1  ...` finding argument, with `rounds:M9.1  ...` present only in the WORKTREE. The real script refuses (exit 1); the worktree-read mutant prints WARN + ok and exits 0.
findings.failure_scenario: The index read is the escape's only narrowing that review.md rule 9 actually names ('an argued entry must be staged -- an unstaged one suppresses a finding while leaving no trace'). Nothing in the suite defends it. The realistic regression is not exotic: any later simplification of :64 to a plain read -- the shape the older finding-argue loop fourteen lines below already uses -- lifts the round cap from a line that exists only in the author's working tree, leaves no trace in the commit, and every one of the five tests stays green. That is the same defect class this task was opened to fix (a promise the code does not keep), one level up, and the row asserts it is covered.

findings.summary: THE ONE PROPERTY THAT JUSTIFIES THE DESIGN IS ASSERTED IN PROSE AND CONSTRAINED BY NOTHING. overTheCapWithASTAGEDArgumentTheGatePasses' own `as()` message says 'an argued round count lands, and -- the point of doing it this way rather than skipping -- the both-roles and no-unresolved-majors checks stay live', and review.md rule 12 now states the same as a standard ('An argued exception keeps both-roles and no-unresolved-majors enforced'). The test stages a verdict pair with `findings: []`, so the no-unresolved-majors loop at check-reviewed.sh:82-106 cannot distinguish running from not running. Surviving mutation, named: insert `finish` immediately after the `warn` at check-reviewed.sh:79. All five tests stay green, and the argued path becomes byte-for-byte equivalent to the `SKIP=check-reviewed` it is documented as being stricter than. (I verified by hand that the code as written DOES keep both checks live -- an argued cap plus a blocking finding exits 1 with 'reviewer: 1 blocking/major finding(s) neither fixed nor argued', and both-roles is enforced at :27-34 before the cap block. The behaviour is right; only the evidence is missing.)
findings.failure_scenario: A later reader shortens the argued branch to `warn ...; finish` -- a plausible tidy-up, since every other early exit in this file finishes -- and the escape silently degrades into a full SKIP: a commit with an unresolved blocking finding lands, the gate prints WARN and ok, pre-commit shows 'Passed', and the standard that says otherwise is still on disk. Non-negotiable 5 is enforced locally only, so nothing downstream notices.

findings.summary: PRE-EXISTING, NOT INTRODUCED HERE, AND NOW CONSPICUOUS: the OLDER finding-argue path in the same script reads the WORKTREE, not the index. Lines 91-98 do `os.path.exists('baselines/review.txt')` / `open(...)`. Measured: a baselines/review.txt that is completely UNTRACKED (`?? baselines/`) containing `reviewer:R1` and `test-reviewer:R1` silences a blocking finding from both roles and the gate prints `ok staged bytes reviewed by reviewer test-reviewer`, exit 0. review.md rule 9 and baselines/review.txt's own header (lines 8-9, 'An entry must be STAGED to count: an unstaged one suppresses a finding while leaving no trace of it') both assert the opposite. This diff fixes exactly that hole for the new `rounds:` key while leaving it open for the heavier one two blocks below, and review.md rule 12's new text reads as though the whole file honours rule 9. Also in the same file: baselines/review.txt's header documents ONE key shape, `<role>:<finding-id>`, and the new `rounds:<task>` key is not documented in the file an author actually edits.
findings.failure_scenario: An author with an unstaged or untracked baselines/review.txt argues away a blocking finding and commits; the gate passes, the commit carries no trace of the finding or the argument, and the finding survives only in gitignored .harness/review/. Fixing it here would widen this task's scope (AGENTS.md 'never widen scope silently'), so the correct outcome is a backlog row naming the index read for the finding path and the header's second key shape -- not an edit to this commit.

findings.summary: THE KEY IS MATCHED AS A REGEX, NOT AS A STRING, SO IT IS SLIGHTLY WIDER THAN 'names the task'. `$TASK` is interpolated unescaped into a BRE. Every task ID in this repository contains a '.', which matches any character. Measured against task M9.1: a line keyed `rounds:M9x1  argued` and one keyed `rounds:M9-1  argued` BOTH lift the cap (WARN + exit 0). And review.sh record performs no validation of --task against the backlog, so a verdict recorded with `--task '.*'` makes any `rounds:<anything> ` line argue it -- measured: `rounds:M9.2  a different task entirely` lifted the cap for task `.*`. Separately, the `[[:space:]]` terminator requires whitespace but not a reason: `rounds:M9.1` followed by a single trailing space or a tab, with no justification at all, is accepted (measured, exit 0), while the bare-key `rounds:M9.1\n` is correctly refused. Everything the task asked me to try to defeat DOES hold: bare `rounds:`, another task's ID, a commented-out line, a leading-whitespace line, `rounds:M9.1extra`, the file staged with the line absent, and the unstaged line are all refused.
findings.failure_scenario: A mistyped key (`rounds:M4-21` for M4.21) is silently accepted as a valid argument, so the author never learns the key was wrong and the greppable record the design depends on -- `grep '^rounds:' baselines/review.txt` -- does not find it. And a whitespace-only entry buys the exception with no stated reason, which is the one thing the entry exists to carry. Both close with one line: `awk -v k="rounds:$TASK" '$1==k && NF>1'` instead of the interpolated grep -- an exact-field compare that also requires a justification.

findings.summary: THE WARN IS INVISIBLE IN THE WORKFLOW THAT PRODUCES IT. pre-commit prints a hook's stdout only when the hook FAILS, unless the hook sets `verbose: true`. Verified two ways: `grep -n verbose .pre-commit-config.yaml` matches nothing, and `pre-commit run check-license-headers` printed only '...Passed' while that script's own `ok` line was swallowed. So on the argued path the gate exits 0 and `git commit` shows a plain green 'Passed' -- the WARN line, and the '(round 3 of 2)' in the success line at :109, are both discarded at exactly the moment a cap breach is being waved through.
findings.failure_scenario: The exception's runtime signal never reaches a human or a log. The durable trace (the staged baseline line, reviewed like any other diff) does survive, which is why this is minor rather than major -- but if the WARN is meant to be the alarm, the check-reviewed hook needs `verbose: true` at .pre-commit-config.yaml:143-149, otherwise an argued third round is indistinguishable from a clean two-round pass in the terminal and in any CI log that runs the hook.

findings.summary: TWO COMMENTS IN THE FIXTURE GIVE TWO DIFFERENT REASONS FOR THE SAME FACT, AND NEITHER IS OPERATIVE. :77-78 says 'A DOCS-ONLY diff, so only the `reviewer` role is required'; :96-99 says the opposite, 'BOTH ROLES, for every round. A `baselines/` path summons the test-reviewer as well'. Measured: `scratch()` copies only check-reviewed.sh, review_rounds.py and lib.sh (:67), so scripts/review-roles.sh does not exist in the scratch repo, REQUIRED_ROLES falls through to the both-roles fallback at check-reviewed.sh:25-26, and the role derivation never runs at all. Reproduced: the test's exact scratch with a docs-only staged diff and only a `reviewer` verdict fails with 'no test-reviewer verdict', regardless of what the diff touches. (With review-roles.sh present the same docs-only diff does require only `reviewer` -- so :77 describes the real gate and not the fixture.)
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer trusting :77-78 removes the test-reviewer verdict from the fixture loop at :106-108 and gets 'no test-reviewer verdict for the staged bytes' -- a failure both comments deny is possible. Worse for the tests' meaning: the suite silently exercises the broken-deriver FALLBACK rather than the derived-roles path, so the comment at :96 that reads as an assertion about role derivation constrains nothing.

findings.summary: review_rounds.py NOW HAS ITS FIRST TESTS AND ITS DOCSTRING STILL CLAIMS A BEHAVIOUR THE CODE DOES NOT HAVE. Lines 11-14: 'A hash whose diff differs from an earlier reviewed one ONLY by baselines/review.txt is not a new round ... counting it would make arguing cost the very round it is arguing about, and the escape hatch would be unusable.' `rounds_for` contains no such exclusion -- it adds every distinct `diff_sha256` for the task to a set and returns its size (lines 32-40). Pre-existing, but directly load-bearing for THIS change: staging the `rounds:` line moves the staged hash, which invalidates both verdicts and forces a fresh round from both roles, so arguing the cap does cost a round, exactly as that paragraph says it must not. It happens to be harmless because the argued branch ignores the count entirely -- but the docstring is the reason a reader would believe the counter is safe to trust. Also inconsistent with the diff: this file says rule 12 'was violated on 7 of 12 tasks', while check-reviewed.sh:37 and the new review.md text both say 8 of 12.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer relies on the documented exclusion when reasoning about a future rule-12 change -- e.g. making the escape depend on the round count, or pruning .harness/review -- and gets a count one or two higher than the docstring implies. And the 7-vs-8 split means whichever number a reader quotes, the other file contradicts it, in the same mechanism the new standard text cites as its evidence.

notes: SCOPE: reviewed scripts/check-reviewed.sh, scripts/review_rounds.py, buildSrc/src/test/java/binjava/ReviewRoundCapTest.java, docs/internal/standards/review.md rule 12 and the M4.21 backlog row. docs/internal/product/decisions/0029-seal-the-chain-you-inherit-from.md is untracked and was not read. WHAT I VERIFIED RATHER THAN TRUSTED, by building scratch repositories from the working-tree scripts and running the gate: the escape refuses a bare `rounds:` line, another task's ID, a commented-out line, a leading-whitespace line, `rounds:<task>extra`, the file staged with the line absent, the key with no whitespace after it, and an unstaged line -- eight rejections, all correct; it accepts a staged `rounds:<task>  <reason>` line and, on that path, STILL enforces both-roles-present (measured: missing test-reviewer verdict exits 1) and no-unresolved-majors (measured: an argued cap plus a blocking finding exits 1). The design's central claim is true in the code; findings 2 and 3 are that nothing in the suite holds it there. review_rounds.py --task behaves on an empty review dir (prints an empty line, and the `[ -n "$TASK" ]` guard covers it), resolves the task from THIS hash's own verdict files so several tasks in the directory cannot cross-talk, and tolerates `--task` before or after the sha; with no arguments it raises IndexError, which the gate's 2>/dev/null swallows as before. COST: no object-store request path is touched -- this is harness enforcement plus documentation, and no billed request rate moves, so the request-rate lens is not engaged. TWO PROCESS OBSERVATIONS. (1) The packet reports check-module.sh FAILED (sequencer and ingest builds), and the packet's own text says a review should not be spent while a deterministic gate is red; the failure comes from unstaged sequencer sources outside this change, so it does not implicate the staged bytes, but it was not fixed before the review was requested. (2) The tree was NOT quiescent during this review: my first `git status` showed sequencer/src/main/java/binjava/sequencer/CommitLog.java modified-unstaged, and a later `pre-commit run` (which I used only to confirm that a passing hook's stdout is suppressed) stashed and restored a DIFFERENT unstaged change -- a mutation probe, `String pod = "pod" + (random.nextInt(pods) * 0);`, in sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/CommitProtocolSimulation.java -- which was gone again moments later. Another agent is mutating the tree concurrently. The five STAGED paths and their hash (d7070bae...) were identical at the start and the end of my run, so this verdict is bound to the bytes I read, but running `pre-commit run` was a mistake on a shared tree and may have perturbed the other run; I made no edit to any tracked file and all probes were built and mutated under the scratchpad.
